newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Croats walk out of Sarajevo cantonal assembly.
newsitem.headline: Croats walk out of Sarajevo cantonal assembly.

text.p: Bosnian Croats walked out of a session of Sarajevo's newly-elected cantonal assembly over the weekend, demanding guarantees from the main Moslem party to protect the rights of the city's Croat community.
The move illustrated the poor state of relations inside Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation, which has failed to make political progress since it was founded two years ago.

Local media reported on Sunday that three Croat deputies elected to the cantonal assembly signed an inaugural oath on Saturday but then walked out of the session to show their dissatisfaction with Moslem authorities.

The main nationalist Croat party (HDZ) issued a statement insisting the Moslem nationalist Party of Democratic Action (SDA) agree a power-sharing deal that would safeguard Croat interests in the Bosnian capital.

"Because we have no assurances that the vital interests of Sarajevo's Croats will be protected and because we do not know that Croat representatives will have any influence in bringing up important decisions, we do not want formally to participate in the work of such a assembly until conditions are fulfilled."

Croats comprise some seven percent of the population in Sarajevo but want a power-sharing arrangement that would allow them to retain some political influence in the predominantly Moslem city, which is the capital of Bosnia as well as the Moslem-Croat federation.
The SDA won a commanding majority in the Sarajevo assembly race, gaining 28 out of 45 deputies in the September 14 elections.
Across the federation, local Croat and Moslem authorities have tended to block power-sharing agreements or the return of refugees.
The southwestern city of Mostar remains strictly divided along ethnic lines despite international pressure on the dominant Croat faction to reunify the town.
Croats and Moslems fought a 10-month war for territory during the Bosnian conflict until the United States pressed them into the federation.
Under the Dayton peace accord, Bosnia is preserved as a loose union of Moslem-Croat and Serb territories.
